items.correction: Each point (xi,yi) yields the constraint b=yi-m*xi. For the shown (1,1) and (3,3), these are b=1-m and b=3-3*m. They are two distinct parameter-space lines meeting at (m,b)=(1,0). items.finding: The diagrams do not imply that adding collinear points creates conflicting/diverging parameter lines, or that every four-point set shares one solution.
items.correction: The shown collinear (1,1),(3,3),(-2,-2) constrain the same line y=x and thus their (m,b) constraint lines share (1,0). A non-collinear point such as (1,-1) does not satisfy y=x, so all four constraints do not share a common point. items.finding: For x*cos(theta)+y*sin(theta)=rho, vertical lines do not have normal angle pi/2. The (theta,rho) voting locus is not a circular arc.
items.correction: For a vertical line x=c, the y coefficient vanishes: sin(theta)=0, so theta=0 modulo pi, with the corresponding signed rho. For a horizontal line, theta=pi/2 modulo pi. A fixed image point (x0,y0) gives rho(theta)=x0*cos(theta)+y0*sin(theta), a sinusoid in the (theta,rho) plane. A single geometric line corresponds to a parameter point after a convention is selected; the family through a fixed point traces the voting sinusoid. Label the derivation Additional teaching.

items.finding: The polar Hough plots and accumulator use (theta,rho), not (m,b), and adding an outlier does not preserve a common intersection for every point.
items.correction: In the polar plot each point generates the sinusoid rho(theta)=x*cos(theta)+y*sin(theta). Collinear points' curves meet at the common line parameters; an outlier generally does not share that peak. Page60 initializes H, loops over each edge point and sampled theta, computes rho, increments H(theta,rho), then finds local maxima and recovers the line equation. Preserve the source warning that image origin is top-left. Do not call these sinusoidal curves (m,b) pairs or assert all four illustrated points are collinear.
